newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures posted gains for the six consecutive session to settle at their highest level since February 2, 1994, after U.S. economic reports allayed fears of an interest rate rise and a favourable European economic backdrop continued to attract cash buyers.
The March bond future rallied from 129.66 to a peak of 130.18, just shy of the 130.20 contract high, after a December U.S. consumer price report showed inflation remained tame.
Traders said although domestic investors were still somewhat shy of investing heavily in cash bonds, there was continued interest in stripped 2023 OATs, notably from non-residents.

"The (U.S.) CPI was good and European economic fundamentals remain weakish, which is positive for bond markets," Valerie Plagnol, economist at Credit Commercial de France, said. The 10-year spread between French and German bond yields, using the the 6.50 percent 2006 OAT and the January 2007 Bund, moved to minus 15 basis points.

Bond traders also said there had been some selling of shorter-dated bonds, maturing between 1998 and 2002, probably to make room for the 21 to 23 billion francs of BTANs the Treasury will be offering at auction on Thursday. The two-year spread between French and German bonds widened slightly.

"The fundamentals in Europe are favourable for a decline in long-term yields, with inflation weak and an imbalance between savings and investment which strongly favours savings," Caroline Newhouse-Cohen, economist at Louis Dreyfus Finance, said.
"The only worry came from the United States and the consumer price index has cleared the ground," she said.

Cohen said they remained confident that 10-year German yields would drop to 5.25 percent by the end of the year, and she said it could happen before then. Benchmark 10-year Bund yields were at 5.77 percent on Tuesday, while 10-year French yields fell to 5.62 percent.
Plagnol said CCF expected 10-year French yields to be at 5.50 percent at the end of the first quarter.
A futures trader said the positive backdrop meant the March bond future could soon reach its all-time high of 131.38, hit on January 13, 1994.
March PIBOR recovered from early weakness, which traders attributed to profit taking, to set a record high at 96.83 despite a slightly weaker franc.
Analysts said the first test of the rate cut optimism pervading the short end would come on Thursday when the Bank of France monetary policy council was due to meet.

A poll conducted by Reuters on Monday showed 10 out of 15 economists expected a cut in the intervention rate from 3.15 percent after Thursday's meeting, which will be the first since two new members were appointed to the council.
The appointment of the two new members, both seen as potentially swelling the dovish ranks of the council, fueled hopes for faster rate cuts in France.
Most economists expect the intervention rate, which sets the floor for French money market rates, to be trimmed at least to the same level of the German repo rate, now at three percent.
